body.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the supreme guru <s>Gorakṣanātha</s>.

children.translated_text: Oṃ. I shall speak the <s>Gorakṣaśataka</s>,
for liberation from the bonds of worldly existence,
which produces self-knowledge in people,
the key to the door of discrimination.
This is the ladder to liberation;
this is the deception of death.
When the mind, turned away from delusion,
is attached to the supreme self —
the fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of the <s>Vedas</s>,
whose branches are frequented by the twice-born,
which extinguishes the burning heat of worldly existence —
a good person takes to <s>yoga</s>.
Posture (<s>āsana</s>), breath-control (<s>prāṇasaṃyāma</s>),
withdrawal [of the senses] (<s>pratyāhāra</s>), then concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>),
meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and absorption (<s>samādhi</s>) —
these are the six limbs of <s>yoga</s>.
The postures are as many
as there are species of living beings.
The complete varieties of all these
are known by <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).
Of the eighty-four <s>lakṣas</s> (8.4 million),
one of each has been described.
Then by <s>Śiva</s>, of the seats (<s>pīṭha</s>),
one hundred and sixty have been made.
Of all the postures,
two alone are distinguished:
the first is called <s>siddhāsana</s> (the adept's pose),
the second is <s>kamalāsana</s> (the lotus pose).
Having firmly placed the left heel at the perineum (<s>yoni-sthāna</s>),

children.text: meḍhre pādam athaikam eva niyataṃ kṛtvā samaṃ vigraham
children.translated_text: and placed one foot fixedly upon the phallus, making the body straight,
standing like a pillar with restrained senses and unwavering gaze, looking between the eyebrows —
this, which generates the breaking open of the door to liberation, is called <s>siddhāsana</s>.

children.text: vāmorūpari dakṣiṇaṃ hi caraṇaṃ saṃsthāpya vāmaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Placing the right foot upon the left thigh, and likewise the left

children.text: dakṣorūpari paścimena vidhinā dhṛtvā karābhyāṃ dṛḍham
children.translated_text: upon the right thigh, holding firmly with both hands crossed behind [the back],

children.text: aṅguṣṭhau hṛdaye nidhāya cibukaṃ nāsāgram ālokayed
children.translated_text: pressing the chin to the chest, gazing at the tip of the nose —
this, which removes diseases and disorders, is called <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus pose) for the self-controlled.
The first <s>cakra</s> is <s>ādhāra</s> (the base);
the second is <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>.
In the middle between these two is the <s>yoni-sthāna</s> (place of origin),
called <s>kāmarūpa</s> (the form of desire).
At the place called <s>ādhāra</s>, situated at the anus,
is a four-petaled lotus.
In its center is proclaimed the <s>yoni</s> (source),
called <s>kāmākhyā</s>, venerated by the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected ones).
In the middle of the <s>yoni</s> is the great <s>liṅga</s>,
facing westward (toward the back).
Split like a jewel at the head —
whoever knows this is a knower of <s>yoga</s>.
Shining like molten gold,
flashing like a streak of lightning,
the four-sided citadel of fire
is located below the phallus.
'<s>Sva</s>' (one's own) means <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath);
<s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s> is its abode.
Therefore, by the name <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s>,
the phallus region is designated.
Strung like a jewel on a thread
where the <s>kanda</s> (bulb) [joins] the <s>suṣumṇā</s> —
that <s>cakra</s> in the region of the navel
is called <s>maṇipūraka</s> (filled with jewels).
Above the phallus and below the navel,
the <s>kanda</s>-source is like one's own egg.
There the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) originate,
seventy-two thousand in number.
Among those thousands of <s>nāḍīs</s>,
seventy-two are cited [as important].
Chief among them as carriers of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath),
ten are further remembered.
<s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>,
and <s>Suṣumṇā</s> as the third,
<s>Gāndhārī</s>, <s>Hastijihvā</s>,
<s>Pūṣā</s>, and also <s>Yaśasvinī</s>,
<s>Alambuṣā</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>,
and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> remembered as the tenth.
This wheel made of <s>nāḍīs</s>
should always be known by <s>yogins</s>.
<s>Iḍā</s> is situated on the left side;
<s>Piṅgalā</s> likewise on the right.
<s>Suṣumṇā</s> is in the central region;
<s>Gāndhārī</s> is in the left eye.
<s>Hastijihvā</s> in the right [eye];
<s>Pūṣā</s> in the right ear;
<s>Yaśasvinī</s> in the left ear;
<s>Alambuṣā</s> also at the anus.
<s>Kuhū</s> at the region of the genitals;
<s>Śaṅkhinī</s> at the root-place (<s>mūlasthāna</s>).
Thus established at [their respective] openings,
the ten <s>nāḍīs</s> abide.
They constantly carry <s>prāṇa</s>,
having <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Agni</s> as [their presiding] deities.
<s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s>, and <s>Suṣumṇā</s> —
these three <s>nāḍīs</s> are cited [as the chief].
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Samāna</s>,
<s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Vyāna</s> indeed,
<s>Nāga</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Kṛkara</s>,
<s>Devadatta</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s> —
The five beginning with <s>Nāga</s> are well known;
the five breaths beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s> —
these in the thousands of <s>nāḍīs</s>
move in the form of the living being.
Under the control of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul)
runs downward and upward.
By the left and right paths,
because of its restlessness, it is not seen.
Just as a ball struck on the ground
by a stick bounces upward,
so the <s>jīva</s>, propelled by <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>,
is likewise drawn about.
Just as a hawk tied by a rope,
even though it has flown away, is pulled back,
so the <s>jīva</s>, bound by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
is pulled by <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>.
<s>Apāna</s> pulls [upward]; <s>prāṇa</s>
pulls <s>apāna</s> [downward].
These two are situated above and below —
whoever knows [how to unite] them is a knower of <s>yoga</s>.
Above the <s>kanda</s> (bulb), the <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s> power,
coiled eight-fold,
constantly covers with her mouth
the opening of <s>Brahmadvāra</s> (the door of <s>Brahman</s>).
Awakened by the union with fire,
impelled by the mind and the wind,
taking along the quality of the <s>jīva</s> (soul),
she ascends upward through the <s>suṣumṇā</s>.
The <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal), the <s>namomudrā</s> (bowing seal),
<s>uḍḍiyāna</s> (flying up), <s>jālandhara</s> (net-holder),
and the root-lock (<s>mūlabandha</s>) — whoever knows these,
that <s>yogin</s> is a vessel for attainments (<s>siddhi</s>).

children.text: vakṣo-nyasta-hanur nipīḍya suciraṃ yoniṃ ca vāmāṅghriṇā
children.translated_text: With the chin placed on the chest, pressing the <s>yoni</s> (perineum) firmly with the left heel for a long time,

children.text: hastābhyām avadhāritaṃ prasaritaṃ pādaṃ tathā dakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: holding the right foot extended with both hands,

children.text: āpūrya śvasanena kukṣi-yugalaṃ baddhvā śanai recayed
children.translated_text: filling both sides of the belly with breath, retaining, then slowly exhaling —

children.text: eṣā pātaka-nāśinī sumahatī mudrā nṝṇāṃ procyate
children.translated_text: this exceedingly great <s>mudrā</s> (seal), destroyer of sins, is proclaimed for people.
The tongue entered into
the hollow of the skull, turned backward,
the gaze directed between the eyebrows —
this <s>mudrā</s> is called <s>khecarī</s> (moving in space).
Above the phallus and below the navel —
they call this <s>uḍḍiyāna</s> (flying up).
The victory of <s>uḍḍiyāna</s> [is] a lock (<s>bandha</s>)
[that is] a lion to the elephant of death.
When <s>jālandhara bandha</s> is performed,
characterized by the contraction of the throat,
neither does the nectar fall into the [digestive] fire,
nor does the breath become agitated.
Pressing the perineum with the heel,
one should contract the <s>yoni</s> [and] the anus.
Drawing <s>apāna</s> upward —
this is called the root-lock (<s>mūlabandha</s>).
Since even <s>Brahmā</s>, out of fear of death,
is devoted to <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control),
as are <s>yogins</s> and sages —
therefore one should restrain the breath.
When the breath (<s>vāta</s>) moves, everything moves;
when it is still, everything becomes still.
The <s>yogin</s> attains the state of being like a pillar —
therefore one should restrain the breath.
The breath (<s>haṃsa</s>) travels outward
a distance of thirty-six finger-breadths,
by the left and right paths —
therefore it is called <s>prāṇa</s>.
Seated in the lotus posture (<s>padmāsana</s>), the <s>yogin</s>,
having bowed to the guru <s>Śiva</s>,
alone, with the gaze fixed on the tip of the nose,
should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control).
<s>Prāṇa</s> is the breath situated in the body;
its restraint (<s>āyāma</s>) is <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
A <s>mātrā</s> (unit) consists of one breath cycle —
by that, the <s>yogin</s> reaches the sky.
Seated in the lotus posture, the <s>yogin</s>
should fill [the body] with breath through the moon [left nostril].
Having retained [it] according to one's ability,
one should exhale again through the sun [right nostril].
Meditating on the disc of the moon —
resembling an ocean of nectar, with the luster of white milk —
in <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, one becomes happy.
Drawing the breath in through the sun [right nostril],
one should fill the belly slowly.
Having retained [it] according to the prescribed method,
one should exhale again through the moon [left nostril].
Meditating on the disc of the sun
as a blazing mass of flaming fire,
situated at the navel — the <s>yogin</s>
in <s>prāṇāyāma</s> becomes happy.
Exhalation (<s>recaka</s>), inhalation (<s>pūraka</s>),
and retention (<s>kumbhaka</s>), whose nature is <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) —
<s>prāṇāyāma</s> is of three kinds,
accompanied by twelve <s>mātrās</s> (measures).
Twelve <s>mātrās</s> in the lowest [grade];
in the middle, double that;
in the highest, triple the <s>mātrās</s> —
this is the determination of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>.
In the lowest [grade], profuse sweating;
in the middle, trembling occurs;
in the highest, the <s>yogin</s> rises [from the ground]
repeatedly while seated in the lotus posture.
Rubbing the limbs is recommended
with the moisture produced by exertion.
Avoiding pungent, sour, and salty [foods],
one should adopt a milk-based diet.
One should inhale the breath gently, gently,
and release it gently, gently.
One should not retain the breath excessively,
nor release it too quickly.
Drawing the <s>apāna</s> upward,
one should unite the breath with <s>prāṇa</s>.
Conducted to the crown of the head by [<s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>] power,
one is freed from all sins.
<s>Prāṇāyāma</s> is thus
the destroyer of the fuel of sins,
the great bridge across the ocean of faults —
so it is always proclaimed by <s>yogins</s>.
By posture (<s>āsana</s>) one destroys diseases;
by <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, sins;
the <s>yogin</s> [destroys] mental disturbances
always through withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>).
The stream consisting of the nectar of the moon
is withdrawn by the sun.
That withdrawal of it —
that is called <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal).
One woman is enjoyed by two,
she who has come from the lunar disc.
The third, who is [produced] from those two —
he becomes free from aging and death.
In the region of the navel is one [force] —
the sun, whose nature is fire.
The moon, whose nature is nectar, is permanently situated
at the root of the palate.
The moon rains downward [with its face down];
the sun consumes upward [with its face up].
One should know the technique
by which the nectar is obtained.
The navel is above [and] the palate below;
the sun is above [and] the moon below.
The technique called 'inverted' (<s>viparīta</s>)
is obtained from the mouth of the guru.
Where the bull (<s>vṛṣa</s>), bound in three ways,
makes the great sound like a roar —
that <s>cakra</s> called <s>anāhata</s> (unstruck)
at the heart, the <s>yogins</s> know.
Having transcended the <s>anāhata</s> [cakra],
and having reached the <s>maṇipūraka</s>,
when the breath reaches the great lotus (<s>mahāpadma</s>) —
the <s>yogin's</s> state becomes immortal.
The syllable 'vi' [in <s>viśuddha</s>] is remembered as <s>haṃsa</s> (the swan);
'stainless' and 'pure' it is called.
Therefore at the throat, the <s>cakra</s> named <s>viśuddha</s>
is known by the knowers of <s>cakras</s>.
In the supreme <s>viśuddha cakra</s>,
having held the water of the lunar digit (<s>soma-kalā</s>),
within a month it does not diminish,
having deceived the mouth of the sun (<s>Ravi</s>).
Having pressed with the tip of the tongue
the great cavity of the royal tooth (<s>rāja-danta-bila</s>),
meditating on the goddess made of nectar (<s>amṛta</s>),
within six months one becomes a poet (<s>kavi</s>).
For the <s>yogin</s> whose body is filled with nectar (<s>amṛta</s>),
after two or three years,
the semen moves upward,
and the powers beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> (becoming minute) arise.
Just as fire [does not abandon] fuel,
and a lamp [does not abandon] its oil-wick,
so the embodied one, filled with the lunar digit (<s>soma-kalā</s>),
does not abandon the body.
Endowed with <s>āsana</s> (posture),
joined with <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control),
united with <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses),
one should practice <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration).
In the heart, the <s>dhāraṇā</s> of the five elements (<s>pañca-bhūta</s>)
should be performed separately, one by one.
Through the steadiness of the mind,
<s>dhāraṇā</s> is accomplished.
The earth (<s>pṛthvī</s>), beautiful like the region of orpiment, yellow, accompanied by the syllable 'la,'

children.text: saṃyuktā kamalāsanena hi catuṣkoṇā hṛdi sthāyinī
children.translated_text: conjoined with <s>Brahmā</s> seated on the lotus, four-cornered, abiding in the heart —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing <s>prāṇa</s> there for five <s>ghaṭikās</s> (periods), one should hold [it] with mind concentrated.

children.text: eṣā stambhakarī sadā kṣitijayaṃ kuryād bhuvo dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the earth-<s>dhāraṇā</s>, which produces immobilization and always grants conquest of the earth.
Resembling a half-moon, white as jasmine, the water-element (<s>ambu-tattva</s>) abides in the throat,
that which, accompanied by the nectar-[like] seed-syllable 'va,' is always conjoined with <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing <s>prāṇa</s> there for five <s>ghaṭikās</s>, one should hold [it] with mind concentrated.
This is the water-<s>dhāraṇā</s>, which neutralizes even the most unbearable deadly poison (<s>kālakūṭa</s>).
That element situated at the palate, resembling the <s>indragopa</s> (cochineal insect), blazing and triangular,
consisting of fire and the syllable 'ra,' beautiful like coral, conjoined with <s>Rudra</s> —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing <s>prāṇa</s> there for five <s>ghaṭikās</s>, one should hold [it] with mind concentrated.

children.text: eṣā vahni-jayaṃ sadā vidadhate vaiśvānarī dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (fire) <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which always grants conquest over fire.

children.text: yad bhinnāñjana-puñja-sānnibham idaṃ tattvaṃ bhruvor antare
children.translated_text: That element resembling a mass of split collyrium (<s>bhinnāñjana</s>), situated between the eyebrows,
circular, consisting of air (<s>vāyu</s>), accompanied by the syllable 'ya,' where <s>Īśvara</s> is the deity —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing <s>prāṇa</s> there for five <s>ghaṭikās</s>, one should hold [it] with mind concentrated.

children.text: eṣā khe gamanaṃ karoti yamināṃ syād vāyavī dhāraṇā
children.translated_text: This is the air-<s>dhāraṇā</s>, which grants <s>yogins</s> the power of moving through the sky.
The space (<s>ākāśa</s>), resembling supremely pure water, situated at the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (crown aperture),
there, conjoined with the eternal <s>Sadāśiva</s>, peaceful, with the syllable 'ha' —

children.text: prāṇaṃ tatra vinīya pañca-ghaṭikāś cittānvitaṃ dhārayed
children.translated_text: directing <s>prāṇa</s> there for five <s>ghaṭikās</s>, one should hold [it] with mind concentrated.
This is the space-<s>dhāraṇā</s>, declared to be skilled at breaking open the door of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>).
Immobilizing (<s>stambhanī</s>), liquefying (<s>drāvaṇī</s>),
burning (<s>dahanī</s>), whirling (<s>bhrāmaṇī</s>),
and desiccating (<s>śoṣaṇī</s>) — thus
are the five <s>dhāraṇās</s> of the elements.
By action, by mind, and by speech,
the five <s>dhāraṇās</s> are difficult to attain.
The <s>yogin</s> who constantly performs them
is released from all sins.
Everything that revolves in thought
abides in the heart of the <s>yogin</s>.
That consciousness which is fixed on the essential reality (<s>tattva</s>) —
that they call meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>).
That meditation is of two kinds:
with qualities (<s>saguṇa</s>) and without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>).
The <s>saguṇa</s> is distinguished by [differences of] color;
the <s>nirguṇa</s>, they know as the Absolute (<s>kevala</s>) alone.
The first <s>cakra</s> is the <s>Ādhāra</s> (base),
resembling molten gold.
Fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose,
meditating [on it], one is released from sin.
The second is the <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>,
beautifully radiant like a fine ruby.
Fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose,
meditating [on it], one is released from transgression.
Resembling the rising sun,
is the <s>Maṇipūraka</s> <s>cakra</s>.
Fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose,
meditating [on it], one shakes the world.
At the lotus of the heart, with the brilliance of lightning,
through the varieties of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,
fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose,
meditating [on it], one becomes one with <s>Brahman</s>.
Constantly in the middle of the bell (<s>ghaṇṭikā</s>),
the <s>Viśuddha</s> [<s>cakra</s>], source of nectar (<s>amṛta</s>) —
fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose,
meditating [on it], one becomes one with <s>Brahman</s>.
The deity situated between the eyebrows,
resembling a lustrous pearl —
fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose,
meditating [on it], one becomes full of bliss (<s>ānandamaya</s>).
Without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), auspicious (<s>Śiva</s>), peaceful,
in the sky, facing all directions —
fixing the gaze on the tip of the nose,
meditating [on it], one is released from suffering.
The anus, the genitals, the navel,
the lotus of the heart, and above that,
the bell (<s>ghaṇṭikā</s>), the site of the uvula (<s>lambikā</s>),
between the eyebrows — the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>).
Stainless, having the form of the sky,
resembling the water of a mirage —
meditating on the Self as all-pervading,
the <s>yogin</s> attains <s>yoga</s>.
As these meditation seats (<s>dhyāna-sthāna</s>)
of <s>yogins</s> have been described,
endowed with limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) and essential reality (<s>tattva</s>),
they produce the arising of the eight powers.
Limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) and essential reality (<s>tattva</s>) —
these two are thus declared.
The limiting adjunct is said to be color (form),
the essential reality is called the Self (<s>ātman</s>).
The limiting adjunct is false knowledge;
the essential reality abides otherwise [as it truly is].
Through constant practice by <s>yogins</s>,
all limiting adjuncts are destroyed.
A crystal gem is seen
as having the color of the Self [reflected in it];
when freed from the distinction of [reflected] power (<s>śakti</s>),
that very Self is praised.
Free from affliction, without support,
beyond phenomenal proliferation, without refuge,
free from disease, without form —
those who know the essential reality know [it as] the essential reality (<s>tattva</s>).
The five sensory objects (<s>mātrā</s>) beginning with sound,
as long as they are recalled in the ears and other [senses] —
that long is it remembered as meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>);
<s>samādhi</s> is beyond that.
When <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is dissolved,
and the mind is absorbed,
then the unity of equal flavor (<s>samarasa</s>) —
that is called <s>samādhi</s>.
<s>Dhāraṇā</s> lasts five <s>nāḍīs</s> (breath-units),
meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) sixty <s>nāḍikās</s>,
and with twelve days [of practice],
<s>samādhi</s> is the restraint of <s>prāṇa</s>.
Neither smell, nor taste, nor form,
nor touch, nor sound —
neither self nor other does the <s>yogin</s> know
who is united in <s>samādhi</s>.
Not consumed by time,
not afflicted by <s>karma</s>,
not mastered by anyone —
the <s>yogin</s> united in <s>samādhi</s>.
Stainless, immovable, eternal,
actionless, without qualities, great,
sky-consciousness, bliss —
those who know <s>Brahman</s> know <s>Brahman</s>.
As milk in milk, as ghee in butter,
as fire deposited in fire —
one should always enter into non-duality;
the knower of <s>yoga</s> [attains] the supreme state.
In the forest of the fear of worldly existence, [<s>yoga</s> is] a fire;
on the stairway-path to liberation —
one should always enter into non-duality;
the knower of <s>yoga</s> [attains] the supreme state.
